headline: Vaccines Have Saved 51.2 Million Lives Across Africa
meta_description: Over 50 years, immunisation programmes in Africa have prevented 51.2 million deaths, with each infant life representing nearly 60 years gained.
summary_short: Vaccination campaigns across Africa have saved an estimated 51.2 million lives over five decades, giving countless children a full lifespan.
body:
Vaccines have saved an estimated 51.2 million lives across Africa over the past 50 years, according to new analysis of immunisation impact.

Each infant life saved through vaccination represents nearly 60 years of life gained—a profound measure of the programmes' human impact. Modern immunisation efforts now protect African children against 13 different diseases, vastly expanding the scope of protection beyond earlier vaccination campaigns.

These figures underscore how sustained investment in public health infrastructure transforms entire populations. What began as targeted disease prevention has evolved into comprehensive immunisation networks that reach millions of families, preventing not just individual deaths but securing generations of healthier, longer lives across the continent.
